issues: Moderate hypoglycemia burden with 5.1% time below 70 mg/dL, including overnight and early morning dips (hours 00:00-02:00 up to 18.5% below range).
Total absence of logged carbohydrate entries in Nightscout, causing reliance on UAM and automated SMBs for postprandial management.
Flat single-segment ISF of 56 mg/dL/U across all 24 hours, failing to account for circadian insulin sensitivity variations.
summary: Analysis of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS configuration shows strong overall time in range (86.0%) and high data completeness (98.7% coverage). However, a 5.1% time-below-range burden is present, driven by nocturnal and early-morning hypoglycemia clusters. Closed-loop automation (SMB/UAM) handles postprandial excursions effectively, but unlogged carbohydrate entries and a flat 24-hour ISF contribute to insulin stacking and delayed containment.
education: A flat ISF across 24 hours can cause over-delivery of correction insulin during periods of high physiological sensitivity, such as overnight or early morning.
Consistent carbohydrate logging enables AAPS to use appropriate carb ratios and pre-boluses, reducing reliance on reactive UAM and microboluses.
strengths: High CGM data quality and completeness with 98.7% coverage and robust loop uptime.
Strong overall Time in Range of 86.0% with effective automated mitigation of postprandial spikes via UAM and SMBs.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.

analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries over 14 days (98.7% coverage, 10 minor gaps with largest at 65 minutes).
analysis_steps.findings: Data quality is good and sufficient for reliable closed-loop and glycemic telemetry analysis.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero recorded carb treatment entries in the dataset.

analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, standard deviation 39.7 mg/dL, CV 32.6%, TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%.
analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic variability is moderate, but TBR of 5.1% with frequent lows down to 41-42 mg/dL requires careful review of overnight basal and ISF.

analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local averages show overnight dips (hours 00:00-02:00 with up to 18.5% below 70 mg/dL) under active basal of 0.6 U/h and a target of 90 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal and tight target settings contribute to nocturnal hypoglycemia clusters when combined with a potent flat ISF.

analysis_steps.evidence: Flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U across all 24 hours; DIA set to 10 hours; varied CR segments between 10.5 and 13.2 g/U.
analysis_steps.findings: A single flat ISF segment does not reflect circadian sensitivity variations and risks over-delivering insulin during high sensitivity windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of explicit carbohydrate entries limits direct evaluation of CR accuracy.

analysis_steps.findings: Automation successfully manages unannounced excursions via UAM and SMBs, but reactive dosing without meal entry contributes to stacking.

analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true (70% adjustment factor), max_basal=12 U/h, max_iob=25 U.
analysis_steps.findings: Automation settings are operating safely within defined limits, with Dynamic ISF actively responding to glucose volatility.

analysis_steps.evidence: 655 insulin entries totaling 275.95 U, zero carb entries, empty meal strategies list in analysis_context.
analysis_steps.findings: Meal management relies entirely on reactive UAM and SMB microbolusing due to unlogged carbohydrate intake.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No logged carbohydrate or prebolus data.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carbs or extended carbs used in the dataset; standard absorption parameters are active.

analysis_steps.findings: Identified that nocturnal hypoglycemia is driven by flat ISF and tight targets, while meal management lacks explicit carb entries. Recommended sequential verification starting with basal/target review.

exceptions.suggestion: Log all carbohydrate intake promptly with standard pre-meal boluses.

meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log accurate carbohydrate amounts and pre-meal bolus times for 3 to 5 consecutive days to evaluate postprandial and late-phase glucose responses.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: In the complete absence of logged carbohydrate entries, meal management relies entirely on reactive UAM and SMBs, leading to delayed containment and increased late-phase hypoglycemia risk.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Introduce consistent manual carbohydrate logging and pre-bolusing for all meals to allow AAPS to utilize proper CR and reduce reliance on reactive UAM microbolusing.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Initiate consistent manual carbohydrate logging and pre-bolusing for all meals over the next 3 to 5 days.
Step 2: Monitor overnight glucose trends and time-below-range to assess whether nocturnal hypoglycemia persists once meals are formally announced.
Step 3: Review telemetry with the care team before considering any adjustments to basal rates, target segments, or ISF.
